guide_enrichment.narrative:
Our numbers are slightly more favorable to Illinois than the market, but the football matchup makes that disagreement difficult to press. Ohio State’s passing efficiency meets an Illinois pass defense that has struggled by our measures. Julian Sayin returns after completing 77.0 percent of his passes for 3,610 yards and 32 touchdowns in 2025, while Jeremiah Smith entered the season with 2,709 career receiving yards and 29 touchdowns. We see clear potential for Ohio State to create explosive separation through the air.

The more interesting question is whether Ohio State’s defense can sustain its established standard after losing eight starters from last season’s unit. The opener offered a strong first data point—three points and 165 total yards allowed—but we are not treating one game against Ball State as proof that every transition has been resolved. Even so, our matchup numbers strongly favor Ohio State against the Illinois running game and in preventing scoring opportunities. That combination leaves us with a small model disagreement, not enough value to move beyond a pass.
guide_enrichment.matchup_to_watch:
We are watching Ohio State’s passing offense against the Illinois secondary. Sayin’s accuracy and Smith’s ability to generate high-value plays attack the area where our numbers show Illinois is most vulnerable. Smith caught eight passes for 151 yards and two touchdowns in the first half of the opener, which illustrates the ceiling without guaranteeing the same result here.

For us, Illinois must limit explosive passes and force Ohio State to sustain longer drives. If the Buckeyes consistently create chunk gains through the air, the market’s expectation becomes much easier to justify.

recent_game.fact: Ohio State opened the 2026 season with a 56-3 win over Ball State on Sept. 5.
Ohio State produced 671 total yards against Ball State: 434 passing and 237 rushing.
Ohio State held Ball State to 165 total yards, including 45 rushing yards and 120 passing yards.
Jeremiah Smith caught eight passes for 151 yards and two touchdowns, all in the first half of the opener.
Bo Jackson averaged 9.2 yards per carry in the opener and scored on a career-long 65-yard run.
Ohio State had 14 players record a reception against Ball State.
Ohio State played 21 true freshmen against Ball State; freshman Legend Bey had 100 all-purpose yards and scored on his first career reception.

quarterback.fact: Julian Sayin returns as Ohio State's starting quarterback after completing a national-best 77.0 percent of his passes for 3,610 yards, 32 touchdowns and eight interceptions in 2025.
Sayin has played in 19 career games with 15 starts and has seven career 300-yard passing games.

offensive_personnel.fact: Ohio State returns eight offensive starters: QB Julian Sayin, RB Bo Jackson, WR Jeremiah Smith, WR Brandon Inniss, OT Phillip Daniels, C Carson Hinzman, OG Luke Montgomery and OG Austin Siereveld.
The Buckeyes lost three offensive starters from 2025: OG Tegra Tshabola and tight ends Max Klare and Will Kacmarek.
Ohio State's starting offensive line had combined for 146 games played and 93 starts after the 2026 opener.
Ohio State entered 2026 with 85.8 percent of its qualifying 2025 offensive-line snaps returning, the highest rate among Power Four teams.
Carson Hinzman has 36 career starts, Austin Siereveld has 21, Phillip Daniels has 17 and Luke Montgomery has 17.
Wide receivers Devin McCuin, Kyle Parker and tight end Hunter Welcing joined Ohio State after previous stops at UTSA, LSU and Northwestern, respectively.
Bo Jackson rushed for a team-high 1,090 yards on 179 carries in 2025.
Jeremiah Smith entered the Texas week with 171 career receptions, 2,709 receiving yards and 29 receiving touchdowns.

defensive_personnel.fact: Ohio State returns three defensive starters from 2025: CB Jermaine Mathews Jr., DE Kenyatta Jackson Jr. and safety Jaylen McClain.
Ohio State lost eight defensive starters: DT Tywone Malone Jr., DT Kayden McDonald, DE Caden Curry, LBs Arvell Reese and Sonny Styles, safeties Caleb Downs and Lorenzo Styles, and CB Devin Igbinosun.
Defensive-line transfers include James Smith and Qua Russaw from Alabama, John Walker from UCF and Beau Atkinson from North Carolina.
Linebacker Christian Alliegro transferred from Wisconsin after accumulating 127 career tackles and eight sacks.
Safety Earl Little Jr. transferred from Florida State after leading that team with 76 tackles in 2025.
Kenyatta Jackson Jr. recorded 11 tackles for loss and 6.5 sacks in 2025.
Jaylen McClain made 53 tackles and played 816 defensive snaps in 2025.

coaching_changes.fact: Ohio State's 2026 coordinators are defensive coordinator Matt Patricia, offensive coordinator Arthur Smith and special teams coordinator Robby Discher.
Tyler Bowen is Ohio State's run game coordinator and offensive line coach, while Billy Fessler is the pass game coordinator and quarterbacks coach.

offensive_context.fact: Ohio State entered its second game averaging 56.0 points and 671 total yards per game, with 434 passing yards and 237 rushing yards.
Ohio State converted 45.5 percent of its third downs and scored on every red-zone possession in the opener.
Ohio State was one of two FBS programs to have a 3,500-yard passer, a 1,000-yard receiver and a 1,000-yard rusher in each of the previous two seasons.

defensive_context.fact: Ohio State allowed 9.3 points and 219.1 total yards per game in 2025, ranking first nationally in scoring defense and total defense.
The 2025 defense allowed 129.7 passing yards per game and 8.73 yards per completion.
Since the start of the 2024 season, Ohio State had allowed 37 touchdowns in 31 games and recorded nine games without allowing a touchdown.
In the 2026 opener, Ohio State allowed 3 points, 165 total yards and a 21.4 percent third-down conversion rate.

special_teams.fact: Punter Joe McGuire is Ohio State's returning specialist starter.
Ohio State replaced 2025 starting kicker Jayden Fielding and long snapper John Ferlmann.

other_relevant.fact: Ohio State is scheduled to host Illinois on Sept. 26, 2026.
